definition: Simulates Self-Rewriting Codebases operating for a day.
description:

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where rewrite engines monitoring, codebase logistics redundancy, or proof preservation maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Self-Rewriting Codebases Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Self-Rewriting Codebases: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Self-Rewriting Codebases — codebases that refactor themselves safely.

Phase 1 — Prove (rewrite engines): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (codebase logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (proof preservation): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (change review): codebase hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and enterprises-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
